fixed: Editing a square dialect previews square calls, such as a swing of corners and a promenade, so a wording you set for a square call shows in the preview; it used to show contra figures.

Add figures from text leaves out a phrase label such as A1 at the start of a square dance's line, as it does for a contra dance, so a pasted square no longer reads "A1 Heads forward and back" under the app's own A1 heading.

Reading a Caller's Companion .USR file as English dances, a formation described only in the caller's own words is a square set when those words start with "Square" or name no other shape: "Sicilian circle; square through to start" now stays a Sicilian circle, keeping its words as the description.
With a screen reader, each field of the phrase-structure rows says which row it is in, so rows such as 3*8*2 and 1*4*2 can be told apart.

On a narrow phone with large text, the dance editor's figure list no longer runs off the edge: the beat count warning and the Add figure button wrap, and a figure's beats move below its text when they don't fit beside it.

The Caller's Companion mapping reads a `.USR` English dance's own formation description as a square set only when it starts with "square" or names no other shape; otherwise it keeps the shape it names, with the description as its detail.
